speaker: Ange Postecoglou
quote_text:
Yeah, no, no, not good enough, especially  the first half. We were just, yeah,  
way too passive, you know, allowed sort of  Arsenal to take control of the game and yeah,  
just really disappointed with the way we, you  know, both with and without the ball, sort of  
allowed them to dictate the tempo and. Paid a  price for it. Yeah, second-half was a little bit  
better, but yeah, nowhere near good enough. So  was that a change at hot times out? Yeah, well,  
it wasn't about gaining control, just having a  sort of different, I said different intent in  
our football. It's just not who we are. It's not  the way I set the team up, it's not the way I want  
to play, you know, to to be sitting in there and  allowing Arsenal to play. Yeah, Yeah what I said  
to their tempo just wasn't good enough. You said  to the TV you said. Too many games getting away  
from you and it needs to stop. Can't go up. Well,  you got no choice. You just got to, you know,  
there's there's no magic cure here. You got to  get up tomorrow and work hard and and go into  
Sunday and prepare to, you know, go into battle  and and you know, turn around our fortunes in our  
season. I mean there's there's there's nothing  that's magical that that's going to change this.  
You know, there's always reasons for all these  things to happen, but the reality of it is that  
our results and our, you know, our form in in in  the league has been nowhere near good enough and  
that needs to change. You're looking for excuses  tonight, the first goal they scored. Well, it did,  
it did. But you know, look, I don't want to talk  about referees because and and I think I've got  
to take responsibility for my team. I let the  referees take responsibility for theirs. It  
wasn't a corner, but you know, it's it's how  things are going for us at the moment. But  
that aside, we weren't anywhere near the level  we needed to be in that first half in such a big  
game and and you know, we've got to, we've got  to understand that what we can control is the  
first thing we need to focus on. And you spoke  yesterday about sort of the defence and have  
moments that let you down to see this without  in mind half Australians that second goal and  
what can you do with these lapses? Well, you know,  like I said, that's just that, you know, I think,  
you know, that second goal was just endemic of our  first, the whole first half. Look, irrespective  
of everything else, like I said, we just didn't  play anywhere near the identity I want us to be,  
you know, we. We're an aggressive team with and  without the ball. We've shown that. We showed  
that seven days ago against Liverpool and tonight,  especially in that first forty-five, we just we we  
we were way too, obviously way too passive and  that's that's not acceptable. And then when when  
you do that, then you know these kind of things  creep in. You know, it was a disappointing goal,  
second goal to concede as well. But yeah,  it's not like we were playing anywhere near  
the level we needed to. You know, like I said,  the second-half was a little bit better and we  
certainly caused some more problems with and  without the ball, but it wasn't enough. It's  
difficult to take down positives from Derby's  feed, but 218 year olds can take anything  
from their performance. I I hope not. You know,  I want them disappointed. This can't be accepted  
by anyone at the club. You know, us losing so  many games in a league season is is not right.  
You know, I know we're going through a tough  trot and yes, we are asking for big jobs,  
but you know. I hope they're hurting the 18  year olds as much as anyone else in in terms of,  
you know, us not being able to deliver on on  a big day, big night. OK. Thank you. Thanks.
title: Ange Postecoglou post-match press conference | Arsenal 2-1 Tottenham Hotspur
